scenario.title: Late shipments
scenario.initial_request: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

M-LATE-AT-HANDOVER-RATE.name: Orders flagged late at handover stage
M-LATE-AT-HANDOVER-RATE.numerator: Orders flagged late at handover stage

M-ORDERS-RELEASED-AFTER-PICKUP.name: Orders released by WMS after carrier pickup already occurred

F-01.statement: Pickup-log records show a median pickup delay of 2.0 hours across 60 pickups.

F-02.statement: Order-db's late_orders_by_stage query shows 300 of 1000 orders flagged late at the handover stage.

F-03.statement: WMS release_batch_runs log shows 290 orders released after carrier pickup had already occurred, across 30 job runs with 21 failures.

F-04.statement: The RELEASE-BATCH WMS job failed in 21 of its 30 runs.

F-05.statement: Carrier contract §3 requires that pickup schedule changes proceed only after SH-CAR confirms.

F-06.statement: Pickup-log pickup_by_slot shows all 6 recorded slots (S-0 through S-5) with a delay_h of 2.0.

CL-01.statement: Build a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late

CL-02.statement: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

H-COMMUNICATION-GAP.statement: Parcels are already delayed for known, unavoidable reasons; the real gap is that customers aren't told why, so a chatbot surfacing existing order/pickup/warehouse data would resolve the complaint.

H-WAREHOUSE-PROCESSING-DELAY.statement: Lateness originates inside ORG-1's warehouse (jobs stuck or slow in DA-WMS before handoff to carrier), independent of any customer messaging.

H-HANDOFF-FAILURE.statement: The ORG-1 to ORG-CAR handoff H-PICK is unreliable (unknown delivery_status/semantic_validity), causing parcels to be lost or delayed at the shop-to-carrier boundary.

H-CARRIER-PICKUP-BOTTLENECK.statement: Delays stem from carrier pickup scheduling: schedule changes require SH-CAR confirmation (K-SCHED) and may not be timely, stalling parcels after warehouse readiness.

H-DATA-FRAGMENTATION.statement: No single source currently joins order, warehouse, and pickup data (DA-ORD, DA-WMS, DA-PICK sit in separate orgs with UNKNOWN completeness), so the true cause of any given lateness cannot yet be reliably determined.

H-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE.statement: The RELEASE-BATCH WMS job itself is unreliable (21 of 30 runs failed) and routinely completes after carrier pickup (290 orders), directly causing parcels to miss pickup windows.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Carrier pickup-log provides the first quantified delay figure: a median 2.0-hour delay across 60 pickups at the carrier handoff stage. This gives one data point for comparing where lateness actually accumulates (pickup vs. warehouse vs. order stage) but by itself does not establish pickup as the dominant cause of customer-reported lateness.

Order-db's stage breakdown shows 300 of 1000 orders (30%) are flagged late specifically at the "handover" stage, i.e. the shop-to-carrier boundary, indicating a sizeable share of overall lateness is attributable to this single stage rather than being spread evenly or concentrated elsewhere.

E-03.content: The carrier picks up two hours late, that's why parcels are late.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-LOG (logistics lead) claims the carrier's two-hour-late pickup is the cause of parcel lateness; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder attribution, not new measured data, though the stated delay magnitude matches E-01's measured 2.0-hour median pickup delay.

WMS release-batch job log shows 290 orders were released only after the carrier's pickup had already occurred, and 21 of 30 batch runs failed — a concrete, warehouse-internal release-timing failure, distinct from the carrier simply arriving late.

E-05.content: Carrier contract §3: pickup schedule changes run after SH-CAR confirms.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Carrier contract §3 (E-05) establishes that pickup schedule changes may only proceed after SH-CAR confirms, which is an authoritative procedural rule rather than new evidence about the cause of lateness.

Pickup-log's per-slot breakdown shows all 6 recorded slots (S-0 through S-5) have an identical 2.0-hour pickup delay, indicating the carrier delay is a uniform/systematic offset rather than varying by time slot. This matches the magnitude already in E-01 but contains no order-id or release-timestamp fields, so it cannot by itself crosscheck pickup timing against WMS release timing or resolve U-CARRIER-CONTRIBUTION.

U-JOIN-OVERLAP.question: Do the 300 handover-late orders (E-02) and the 290 WMS-released-after-pickup orders (E-04) refer to the same order population?
U-JOIN-OVERLAP.decision_impact: Determines whether fixing RELEASE-BATCH alone resolves the handover lateness or whether a separate cause contributes to part of the 30%.
U-JOIN-OVERLAP.resolution_path: Run an order-id-level join between DA-WMS release_batch_runs and DA-ORD late_orders_by_stage records.
U-JOIN-OVERLAP.safe_placeholder: Treat the 30% handover-late figure as an upper bound on the fixable WMS-caused lateness until the join is run; do not promise full resolution from a WMS fix alone.

U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE.question: What specifically causes RELEASE-BATCH to fail in 21 of 30 runs?
U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE.decision_impact: Determines which remediation (access, config, capacity) is required and whether it is a quick fix or larger engineering effort.
U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE.resolution_path: Inspect wms-jobs failure/error logs for the 21 failed RELEASE-BATCH runs.
U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE.safe_placeholder: Continue read-only diagnosis via wms-jobs; do not commit to a remediation timeline until failure logs are reviewed.

U-CARRIER-CONTRIBUTION.question: Does the carrier's own 2-hour median pickup delay (E-01) independently add to lateness for orders that WMS released on time?
U-CARRIER-CONTRIBUTION.decision_impact: Determines whether any carrier-facing action (e.g. push_pickup_schedule under K-SCHED) is still needed alongside the WMS fix.
U-CARRIER-CONTRIBUTION.resolution_path: Compare pickup timing against release timing for orders released before pickup to see if carrier delay alone causes lateness.
U-CARRIER-CONTRIBUTION.safe_placeholder: Do not propose pickup schedule changes (K-SCHED) until carrier-only contribution is isolated from the WMS-release effect.

A-RELEASE-FAILURE-CAUSES-LATE.statement: The 21/30 RELEASE-BATCH run failures are the mechanism producing the 290 orders released after pickup, rather than a coincidental or separately caused timing issue.

A-HANDOVER-POPULATION-OVERLAP.statement: The 300 orders flagged late at the handover stage (E-02) substantially overlap with the 290 orders released after pickup by WMS (E-04), i.e. both reflect the same underlying failure rather than two independent lateness sources.

K-SCHED.description: pickup schedule changes need carrier confirmation

DA-PUSH-PICKUP-SCHEDULE.subject: ORG-CAR
conditions: SH-CAR must confirm each pickup schedule change before it takes effect, per carrier contract §3 (E-05)

SC-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.validation_method: Join DA-WMS release_batch_runs records with DA-ORD late_orders_by_stage records by order id and compute overlap percentage.

SC-REDUCE-RELEASE-FAILURES.validation_method: Re-query wms-jobs.release_batch_runs after remediation and recompute failed_runs/runs against the E-04 baseline.

SC-REDUCE-HANDOVER-LATENESS.validation_method: Re-run order-db.late_orders_by_stage after remediation and compare to the E-02 baseline.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Stakeholder SH-CX requested a chatbot that tells customers why their parcel is late (CL-01, initial_request).
symptoms: 30% of orders (300/1000) are flagged late at the handover (shop-to-carrier) stage (E-02).
The RELEASE-BATCH WMS job failed in 21 of its 30 runs (E-04).
290 orders were released by the warehouse only after carrier pickup had already occurred (E-04).
Carrier pickups show a median 2.0-hour delay across 60 pickups (E-01), which SH-LOG attributes as the sole cause (E-03).
problem_definition.root_problem: The WMS RELEASE-BATCH job is unreliable (failed in 21 of 30 runs, E-04) and routinely releases orders only after carrier pickup has already occurred (290 orders, E-04), causing those parcels to miss their pickup window and arrive late. This is a warehouse-internal release-timing failure (H-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE, CONFIRMED), not primarily carrier lateness (H-CARRIER-PICKUP-BOTTLENECK) or a lack of customer communication (H-COMMUNICATION-GAP).

structural_remedies.description: Run a deterministic order-id join between DA-WMS release_batch_runs and DA-ORD late_orders_by_stage using existing read-only tools to resolve U-JOIN-OVERLAP and satisfy SC-CAUSE-CONFIRMED.
structural_remedies.rationale: order-db and wms-jobs are read-only, HEALTHY, and this join is already within PD-1 intended_scope (correlate_late_orders_with_wms_releases); no approval constraint applies.; residual gap: Confirms whether the 300 handover-late and 290 released-after-pickup populations overlap but does not fix the RELEASE-BATCH failures or prevent future late releases.

structural_remedies.description: Formally assign ownership of RELEASE-BATCH job reliability to SH-WMS with a mandated incident-review process to diagnose and remediate the 21/30 run failures.
structural_remedies.rationale: Recording an ownership/process assignment is a documentation change with no protected action or approval requirement attached.; residual gap: Assigning ownership does not itself fix the 21/30 failures; the actual fix still depends on diagnosing U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, which is HIGH criticality and still OPEN.

structural_remedies.description: Add a process/config gate that blocks carrier pickup until RELEASE-BATCH is confirmed successful for the affected orders, directly stopping the release-after-pickup mechanism.
structural_remedies.rationale: The tool_surface exposes wms-jobs as read_only=true with no domain_authorization or protected_action to modify WMS job scheduling, so this change cannot be executed through available tools; it also presupposes a diagnosed fix that U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE (OPEN) has not yet produced.; residual gap: Would require an ORG-1 engineering change outside this harness's tool surface and remaining budget, and is blocked until the specific failure cause is known.

structural_remedies.description: Defer the originally requested customer-facing chatbot (CL-01) since it addresses the communication symptom, not the confirmed warehouse-internal release failure.
structural_remedies.rationale: Deferring a feature is a scoping decision with no tool execution or approval dependency.; residual gap: Customer-facing lateness explanations remain unaddressed until the chatbot is revisited post-fix; H-COMMUNICATION-GAP is only LOW decision_impact so this is an acceptable trade-off for now.

decision_log.rationale: causal chain: The RELEASE-BATCH WMS job fails in 21 of 30 runs (E-04). → When the job fails or lags, orders are released from the warehouse only after the carrier has already completed pickup, affecting 290 orders (E-04). → Those orders miss their scheduled pickup window and must wait for the next cycle, which is recorded as lateness at the handover stage for roughly 30% of orders (E-02). → Customers receive their parcel late and, lacking visibility into the cause, request an explanation (initial request, CL-01).; rejected framings: [('H-COMMUNICATION-GAP', "Supported only by E-01 and E-03 (a stakeholder claim) and mirrors the requester's own requested solution (a chatbot); it does not account for the confirmed warehouse-internal release failure in E-04, so treating it as the root cause would adopt the requested solution's premise rather than test it."), ('H-CARRIER-PICKUP-BOTTLENECK', 'Contradicted by E-04, which shows 290 orders were released only after the carrier had already picked up, meaning warehouse release timing, not carrier lateness, determines when the parcel misses the window.'), ('H-DATA-FRAGMENTATION', 'Already REJECTED in the evidence base; despite UNKNOWN completeness flags on the data assets, E-04 produced a measurable, authoritative figure that contradicts the premise that cause cannot be determined.'), ('H-HANDOFF-FAILURE', 'Already REJECTED; contradicted by E-01, E-03 and E-04, which point to a release-timing failure occurring before the shop-to-carrier handoff rather than an unreliable handoff itself.')]
[CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-JOIN-OVERLAP deferred to VOB-U-JOIN-OVERLAP; [CONDITIONAL] critical unknown U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE deferred to VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE

The other intended_scope items (diagnose_release_batch_failures, correlate_late_orders_with_wms_releases) remain OPEN-VOB-blocked (VOB-U-JOIN-OVERLAP, VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE) and are not in release_scope, so no work items are proposed for them. No protected action (push_pickup_schedule, K-SCHED/DA-PUSH-PICKUP-SCHEDULE) appears in release_scope, so no protected_actions are proposed even though pickup-sched is a mutating tool on the surface. actions.question: At which stage (warehouse processing, carrier pickup, transit) are late orders in DA-ORD currently stalling?
actions.expected_information_gain: Reveals which pipeline stage (warehouse vs carrier vs transit) accounts for most lateness, letting us weight the warehouse, carrier, and data-fragmentation hypotheses against each other.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Determines whether follow-up investigation and any eventual chatbot data source should focus on warehouse, carrier, or cross-org integration work.
actions.why_now: This is the broadest, lowest-cost read-only query available (DA-ORD, AUTHORITATIVE source) and should be run before narrower stage-specific queries to orient which hypotheses to deepen.

actions.question: What do the recorded pickup delays in DA-PICK show about frequency and cause of late carrier pickups, and do they correlate with K-SCHED confirmation timing?
actions.expected_information_gain: Directly tests whether carrier pickup scheduling (tied to the K-SCHED human-approval constraint and the H-PICK handoff) is the actual bottleneck mechanism.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: If pickup delays are frequent and tied to K-SCHED confirmation lag, that justifies next steps around the carrier scheduling constraint rather than warehouse or messaging fixes.
actions.why_now: This catalog item's operation name literally names 'pickup_delays', the exact mechanism H-CARRIER-PICKUP-BOTTLENECK and H-HANDOFF-FAILURE claim, so it is the most direct test available for those two live hypotheses.

actions.question: Do release_batch_runs in DA-WMS show jobs stuck, delayed, or slow before handoff to the carrier?
actions.expected_information_gain: Shows whether warehouse batch-release processing itself is the source of delay, independent of carrier or messaging issues.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: Confirms or rules out an internal ORG-1 warehouse processing root cause, directing whether remediation effort belongs inside the warehouse system.
actions.why_now: This operation literally names the warehouse job release/batch mechanism that H-WAREHOUSE-PROCESSING-DELAY claims is slow, making it the most direct available test for that still-live hypothesis.

actions.question: From the logistics lead's view, what is driving late shipments, is data on cause currently fragmented across orgs, and are customers told the reason when known?
actions.expected_information_gain: Provides a cross-cutting operational view that can corroborate or contradict the data-query findings and specifically probes whether a communication gap (vs. an unresolved root cause) exists.
actions.decision_impact_rationale: The logistics lead is positioned across ORG-1's warehouse and carrier interface and is the only available source that can speak to whether known causes are already being communicated to customers.
actions.why_now: No tool-query catalog item addresses whether existing cause information is actually communicated to customers, so this interview is the only remaining way to directly test H-COMMUNICATION-GAP.

proposal.root_problem: The WMS RELEASE-BATCH job is unreliable (failed in 21 of 30 runs, E-04) and routinely releases orders only after carrier pickup has already occurred (290 orders, E-04), causing those parcels to miss their pickup window and arrive late. This is a warehouse-internal release-timing failure (H-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE, CONFIRMED), not primarily carrier lateness (H-CARRIER-PICKUP-BOTTLENECK) or a lack of customer communication (H-COMMUNICATION-GAP).

symptoms: 30% of orders (300/1000) are flagged late at the handover (shop-to-carrier) stage (E-02).

causal_chain: The RELEASE-BATCH WMS job fails in 21 of 30 runs (E-04).
When the job fails or lags, orders are released from the warehouse only after the carrier has already completed pickup, affecting 290 orders (E-04).
Those orders miss their scheduled pickup window and must wait for the next cycle, which is recorded as lateness at the handover stage for roughly 30% of orders (E-02).
Customers receive their parcel late and, lacking visibility into the cause, request an explanation (initial request, CL-01).

key_points: Original request (CL-01, from SH-CX) was for a chatbot explaining parcel lateness, but investigation reframed the problem: the WMS RELEASE-BATCH job is unreliable (21 of 30 runs failed, E-04) and 290 orders were released only after carrier pickup had already occurred (E-04) — a warehouse-internal release-timing failure, not primarily a communication gap or carrier fault.

Supporting evidence: 30% of orders (300/1000) are flagged late at the handover stage (E-02); carrier pickups show a median 2.0-hour delay across 60 pickups (E-01), uniform across all 6 recorded slots (E-06); SH-LOG attributed lateness to the carrier (E-03), but this is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim, not measured proof of causation.

The hypothesis H-RELEASE-BATCH-FAILURE is CONFIRMED (supported by E-04); H-WAREHOUSE-PROCESSING-DELAY is SUPPORTED; H-CARRIER-PICKUP-BOTTLENECK remains only a CANDIDATE (contradicted by E-04); H-COMMUNICATION-GAP and H-HANDOFF-FAILURE were respectively SUPPORTED(low-impact)/REJECTED and H-DATA-FRAGMENTATION was REJECTED.

The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-impact unknowns (U-JOIN-OVERLAP, U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE) as verification obligations VOB-U-JOIN-OVERLAP and VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE, both still OPEN at release time.

What was actually released: only the crosscheck_pickup_timing_against_releases:DA-PICK scope (matching the plan's minimum_useful_scope and release_scope; work item W-WI-1 is DONE). The diagnose_release_batch_failures:DA-WMS and correlate_late_orders_with_wms_releases:DA-ORD scopes were NOT released because they fall under the two OPEN HIGH-impact VOBs.

Decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (no holds): the gate's open VOBs block scopes that lie outside the actual release scope, so the narrower crosscheck work could proceed while the root-cause diagnosis and population-overlap confirmation remain unresolved and unreleased.
The customer-facing chatbot originally requested (CL-01) was deferred (SR-R-DEFER-CHATBOT) since it would address only the communication symptom, not the confirmed warehouse release-timing failure.

The actual root-cause fix identified (SR-R-PRE-PICKUP-RELEASE-GATE, a gate blocking carrier pickup until RELEASE-BATCH succeeds) was judged infeasible now because wms-jobs access is read-only with no authorization to change scheduling, and the root cause itself is still undiagnosed.
limitations_explained: Two HIGH-impact unknowns remain OPEN as verification obligations (VOB-U-JOIN-OVERLAP, VOB-U-RELEASE-BATCH-ROOT-CAUSE); their blocking_scope sits outside what was released, so the release proceeded, but it means it is still unconfirmed whether the 300 handover-late orders (E-02) and 290 released-after-pickup orders (E-04) are the same population, and the specific cause of the 21/30 RELEASE-BATCH failures (E-04) is not yet diagnosed.

The real fix for the release-after-pickup mechanism — a process/config gate blocking carrier pickup until RELEASE-BATCH succeeds — was not implemented: it is currently infeasible because the wms-jobs tool is read-only with no authorization to alter scheduling, and the underlying root cause is still unknown.
A residual median 2-hour carrier pickup delay (E-01) may continue independently of any WMS-side fix, so warehouse remediation alone would not fully resolve lateness attributable to the carrier.
The diagnose_release_batch_failures:DA-WMS and correlate_late_orders_with_wms_releases:DA-ORD work remains blocked from release by the two OPEN HIGH-impact VOBs described above.

U-CARRIER-CONTRIBUTION (MEDIUM, OPEN, not deferred to a VOB) is unresolved: it is unknown whether the carrier's own 2-hour delay (E-01) independently adds to lateness even for orders WMS released on time, which could bias interpretation of the crosscheck results.

The completeness of DA-WMS and DA-PICK underlying the released crosscheck is marked UNKNOWN in places (DA-ORD completeness is UNKNOWN; DA-WMS/DA-PICK are listed COMPLETE for the datasets used but the summary of unfinished items flags completeness as unverified), so the crosscheck's correctness depends on data whose completeness has not been fully verified.
proposal.summary: The stakeholder-requested solution was a customer-facing chatbot explaining parcel lateness (CL-01, SH-CX), but the problem definition (PD-1) reframed the root problem using measured evidence: the WMS RELEASE-BATCH job failed in 21 of 30 runs and routinely released 290 orders only after carrier pickup had already occurred (E-04), a warehouse-internal release-timing failure, while 300/1000 orders are flagged late at the handover stage (E-02) and carrier pickups show a median 2.0-hour delay (E-01, E-06). The DEFINE gate returned CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring two HIGH-impact unknowns about order-population overlap and RELEASE-BATCH root cause as open verification obligations. Because those obligations block scope outside what was actually released, the harness released only the pickup-timing-vs-release crosscheck (DA-PICK scope, work item W-WI-1 DONE) with decision RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION and no holds; the deeper WMS diagnosis, order-level join, and the originally requested chatbot were deferred or held back pending resolution of open unknowns and infeasible fixes.
